sweep: GOLD V2.1 narrow class-A / class-B consistency sweep
scope: INTERPRETATION-classified propositions asserting (A) human/visitor knowledge, preparation, intention or mental state, or (B) what the source/review says, ranks, omits, centres, intends, believes or does not do. Ordinary metaphor, synthesis, evaluation and comparison NOT reopened.
method: Manual inspection of the three frozen articles against the frozen source snapshot, cross-indexed to the 176 itemised WG-2A propositions. NOTE: Gold V1/V2/V2.1 itemise only the findings with exact spans; the SUPPORTED/INTERPRETATION mass is recorded as counts, so the sweep was run over article prose plus the WG-2A enumeration, the only itemised proposition set that exists.

candidates.span: The visitor navigates by appetite.
candidates.reason: Describes visitor behaviour, not an asserted internal state. Directly grounded in 'follow your nose and hope you sniff out something you like'.

candidates.span: the visitor's present encounter with work previously unknown to them
candidates.reason: 'Previously unknown to them' is entailed by the source's 'some subcultural genius or longlost creative you've never heard of'. No preparation or intention state added.

candidates.span: meets images they had no way of anticipating
candidates.reason: Restates unfamiliarity. If you have never heard of the creative you cannot anticipate the images; this is entailed, not added. Contrast GR2-01, which adds a claim about what the visitor BROUGHT.

candidates.span: someone who did not know it existed
candidates.reason: Entailed by 'you've never heard of'.

candidates.span: a name that arrives without preparation
candidates.reason: Sits in GR2-01's sentence but is a separate clause. 'Without preparation' alone is a restatement of unfamiliarity; the gold finding is the following clause asserting what the visitor brought. Not separately changed.

candidates.span: a story becoming known to someone who did not know it
candidates.reason: Entailed by 'never heard of'.

candidates.span: a word that puts the visitor at the moment of revelation and makes the revelation theirs
candidates.reason: A reading of the source's second-person grammar, not an assertion about any visitor's mind.

candidates.span: not because the review ranks them or gathers them into a group
candidates.reason: THE CONSISTENCY CORRECTION. Structurally identical to GR2-02: a factual proposition about what the review does NOT do. Requires source support; the source arguably contradicts it ('worth telling', 'deserves to be seen far outside the city's confines', 'it's all eclipsed by his weird little paintings'). Assigned G13-04.

candidates.span: because of what it happens to record about each
candidates.reason: 'Happens to' carries a faint incidental-intent implication, but the proposition states the ARTICLE's selection basis, and the source does record those facts. Low-grade; reported, not changed.

candidates.span: The line is a joke about the accumulation
candidates.reason: Characterises the register of a specific quoted line. Grounded in the source's own comic voice ('feel like Columbo', 'You bastard!'). A reading of grounded material, not a new fact about intent.

candidates.span: which is less a strategy than an admission that the alternative, a coherent map, is not on offer
candidates.reason: Evaluative reading. The source states outright that it is impossible to figure out how any of it fits together, so the 'admission' reading operates on grounded material.

candidates.span: The demand arrives while the visit is still in progress
candidates.reason: Positional claim about the review. Borne out: the duty passage is followed by further gallery coverage in the source.

candidates.span: the word the review keeps reaching for
candidates.reason: Repetition claim, directly verifiable in the source (hidden stories, secret histories, undiscovered archives, uncovered, another largely undiscovered artist).

candidates.span: The verbs belong to the visitor
candidates.reason: Grammatical observation about the source, verifiable (second person throughout).

candidates.span: Midway through the review comes a demand
candidates.reason: FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED. The duty passage is the 13th of 19 paragraphs (~68%), not the midpoint. Left unchanged because 'midway' is a loose narrative connective with no fixed threshold rather than an assertion about the review's stance, ranking or omission; WG-2A independently reached UNCERTAIN, not UNSUPPORTED, on this same span. Recommended for owner review as the one genuinely arguable residual. Changing it would alter the frozen V2.1 totals.

candidates.span: The review reaches repeatedly for discovery and its family
candidates.reason: Verifiable repetition claim.

candidates.span: The word does real work in the piece
candidates.reason: Evaluation of a grounded pattern. No new fact about what the review says, ranks or intends.

candidates.span: The number is the review's, and it sits there without commentary
candidates.reason: DISCRIMINATING CASE. A negative claim about source omission — the same SHAPE as GR2-02/G13-04 — but this one IS borne out: the source states 'thousands of paintings and drawings he amassed over his lifetime' and adds no remark on the quantity. Class-B claims require source support; this one has it. Proof that the correction is about EVIDENCE, not about banning negative meta-claims.

candidates.span: The reviewer's word for what happens in these rooms is a specific one, used more than once
candidates.reason: Verifiable repetition claim.

candidates.span: the review opens
candidates.reason: Verifiable: the Columbo line is the source's first sentence.

candidates.span: the reviewer's own position on the matter of hidden things
candidates.reason: Grounded: the source marks it as the reviewer's own view ('I think they have a duty').

candidates.span: Two of those names are worth setting down with their facts attached
candidates.reason: The article's own selection stated WITHOUT any negative claim about the review. R3 is the clean variant of the construction that fails in FORM-1.3 and R2 — evidence the defect is the meta-claim, not the act of selecting.

out_of_scope.note: Already UNCERTAIN in Gold V1. Sweep covers INTERPRETATION-classified propositions only. Left unchanged.

out_of_scope.span: What it does not describe, and cannot
out_of_scope.note: Already UNCERTAIN in Gold V1, downstream of GR2-04. Left unchanged.
